brief:
Lajee Celtic, founded in the Aida refugee camp in the West Bank, has grown into a decade-old football movement attracting international support, Al Jazeera English reported. The club emerged from the camp's youth community and has since cultivated a fanbase that spans continents, drawing admirers including former Manchester United player Eric Cantona.

The club's rise reflects how grassroots Palestinian sports organizations have leveraged football to foster connections beyond their immediate communities. Lajee Celtic's evolution from a local team into a globally recognized symbol demonstrates the sport's capacity to mobilize solidarity networks around Palestinian causes.
dek: The football club founded in a West Bank refugee camp has built a global movement of solidarity.
title: West Bank refugee camp club builds global solidarity through football
